## Triage: p1 · `domain:server` · `area:automation` · **`needs-user-decision`** · 2026-10-29T17:56Z

⛔ Not a claim. This is a security boundary, so the posture is the maintainer's to set. Triage does not set it.

- Read fresh. Both `sys_*` refusals in front of MCP `run_action` are deliberate fail-closed defaults. One of them (`invokeBusinessAction`) is unconditional. Opening them exposes the identity actions (`ban_user`, `set_user_password`, `impersonate_user`, …) to agents.
- **Options for the maintainer:**
  - **A.** Keep both refusals. Identity actions stay human-only, and the #27506 goal is recorded as not covering `sys_*`.
  - **B.** Lift them only for an action that carries the existing per-action AI-exposure flag, default off. The REST door's gates then run unchanged: permissions, the packaged-action switch, and the audit.
  - **C.** Lift them for every `sys_*` action that the REST door serves.
- **Triage's lean: B.** The fail-closed default holds, and the decision becomes per action and explicit.
- No dispatch until the ruling. p1, at the priority of #27506.

Added fact · 2026-10-29T19:52Z · from the dev's round-2 report on PR #27664 (card #27610), checked by the seat on `origin/main`.

The gap is on the listing too, not only on `run_action`'s two refusals: `registerActionTools` in `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` (L1228–L1230) filters `list_actions` with `actions.filter((a) => !a.objectName || !isSystemObject(a.objectName))` unless `allowSystemObjects: true`. A fix that lifts only the `run_action` guards leaves the action invisible to an agent that lists first, so a resolution of this card should name both sites. ADR-0066 D4's Amended note (as amended by #27664) cites this card for both.

Brief-claimed-by: session_01Utp6CbQLcy8yg6vhJVXXi8 · batch #429 · 2026-10-30T01:52Z

Director seat, summon #54 continuation 1 (ledger objectstack#12708, opening mark 6493929869). Presented to the maintainer in batch #429 as item 1 of 3 — a security-boundary posture (triage 6504357275: the maintainer sets it; on the human floor by rule).

Seat increment (re-read at `origin/main` `ded67bfb`, 2026-10-30T01:52Z):
- Premises re-run, all hold: the runtime guard `isSystemObjectName(objectName)` sits at action-execution.ts L3212, **before** the per-action AI-exposure check `actionAiExposureError` at L3225 (the ADR-0011 opt-in `ai: { exposed: true, description }`, action.zod.ts L1626, default off); the MCP side has `allowSystemObjects` (mcp-http-tools.ts L180 / L281 / L695, default false) in front of both `run_action` and the `list_actions` filter (added fact 6506838679); PR #27649 is merged, so the REST door now serves the packaged identity actions on `sys_user` behind the packaged-action switch, the action's permissions and the audit; #27506 (the goal 「agents and humans use one system」) is closed.
- Prior rulings: #27506's ruling C step 2 (the goal), ADR-0011 (AI exposure is per action, opt-in, default off), ADR-0066 D4 as amended by #27664 (cites this card for both sites). `check-prior-rulings.mjs --card 27681` names ADR-0110 D1, ADR-0036 §1, ADR-0063 §2, ADR-0090 D11, ADR-0099 D2, ADR-0106 D6 — term matches, none sets the `sys_*` posture for MCP.
- Facets: agree with triage's lean. ① one system for agents and humans means one set of gates per action, not a second gate keyed on the object's name prefix; the per-action opt-in already exists and is the ADR-0011 shape. ② the pull is the maintainer's own goal on #27506 and the packaged identity actions #27649 just opened over REST. ③ decides the letter: C (lift for every `sys_*` action the REST door serves) makes `ban_user` / `impersonate_user` reachable by any agent the moment REST serves them; B keeps fail-closed and makes each exposure an explicit, reviewable line in the action's own metadata; A leaves the goal unmet with the refusal written down. ④ B adds no key (the `ai` block exists) and no gate; it removes a blanket refusal in favour of the existing per-action one.
- Seat's letter: **B** — a `sys_*` action is reachable over MCP (`list_actions` and `run_action`, both sites) only when the action declares `ai: { exposed: true, … }`; the runtime's unconditional `isSystemObjectName` refusal and the MCP `allowSystemObjects` gate both yield to that flag, and every REST-door gate (packaged-action switch, permissions, destructive confirmation, audit) runs unchanged behind it. Not C (blanket exposure of identity actions to agents), not A (the one-system goal recorded as not covering `sys_*`).
- Workload of B: `domain:server` · 1 PR · S–M (two guards in `packages/runtime` + `packages/mcp`, the `list_actions` filter, a dogfood case on a `sys_user` action) · `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` (no new authorable key; the opt-in exists) · precedent: ADR-0011's exposure check on non-`sys_*` actions.
- After the ruling: triage grades the card into `pm:queue` for `domain:server` (p1) with `Ruling-ref:`; the identity actions' own `ai.exposed` declarations are the app author's (platform-objects) choice per action, not flipped by this ruling.

Prior rulings read: run_action, sys_, allowSystemObjects, AI exposure, ADR-0011 → #27506 C, ADR-0066 D4 (amended); thread: 6504357275, 6506838679; repo: objectstack-ai/objectstack

director#1 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbQLcy8yg6vhJVXXi8

## 席位意见（增量）· 多维度综合分析 · director seat (summon #54 continuation 1, `session_01Utp6CbQLcy8yg6vhJVXXi8`) · on the maintainer's 「27681 多维度综合分析，给我建议」 · 2026-10-30T02:22Z

Brief 6512999526 stands; this comment is the deeper reading the maintainer asked for. ⛔ Not a ruling. Every platform fact below is read at `origin/main` `ded67bfb`.

### Facts measured

- **Who is behind the guard.** Twelve `sys_*` identity objects declare `type: 'api'` actions (`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/`: account, api-key, invitation, member, oauth-application, organization, session, sso-provider, team-member, team, two-factor, user). `sys_user` alone carries ban / unban / set password / impersonate / change email / change password / revoke sessions and more. **None of them declares an `ai:` block** (`grep -l '^\s+ai:\s*\{' … sys-*.object.ts` → 0 files). So today no system action is exposed to agents by declaration either.
- **Two guards, one of them unreachable by any declaration.** `invokeBusinessAction` refuses `isSystemObjectName(objectName)` at action-execution.ts L3212, **before** the ADR-0011 exposure check `actionAiExposureError` at L3225; the MCP bridge's `allowSystemObjects` (mcp-http-tools.ts L180 / L281 / L695, default false) sits in front of `run_action` and the `list_actions` filter (6506838679).
- **The agent is the caller.** The bridge runs every tool as the authenticated principal with the same permission, RLS and audit path as REST `/actions/...` (mcp-http-tools.ts L92, L234; stdio binds `OS_MCP_STDIO_API_KEY`, ADR-0101). After PR #27649 that same principal can call `POST /api/v1/actions/sys_user/ban_user` over HTTP and be served, behind the packaged-action switch (ADR-0126), the action's permissions (ADR-0066 D4) and the audit. **The MCP blanket guard therefore does not keep an agent away from identity actions; it keeps the MCP surface from matching the REST surface for the same key.**
- **The governance already written.** ADR-0011: exposure is opt-in and default off, "the physical boundary between an AI drafted an action and the agent fleet may now run it"; `ai.description` required; permission parity; confirmation parity — destructive actions route through HITL confirmation, `ai.requiresConfirmation` overridable by the author. ADR-0066 D4 as amended 2026-10-29 (ruling 6499781492): one gate, two surfaces; the `sys_*` MCP gap is recorded there and names this card. `impersonate_user` carries a `confirmText` today (sys-user.object.ts L418).

### Seven dimensions

1. **Security boundary and blast radius.** The identity actions split in two: lifecycle acts (ban / unban, revoke a session, cancel an invitation, remove a member) and **credential- or session-minting acts** (impersonate a user, set a password, create or rotate an API key, change an SSO provider). The second group is where an agent mistake or an injected instruction becomes account takeover. A name-prefix guard treats both groups the same and treats `sys_invitation.cancel` like `sys_user.impersonate`; a per-action declaration can tell them apart.
2. **One system for agents and humans** (the maintainer's goal, #27506 / ADR-0066 D4 amendment). A blanket refusal keyed on an object-name prefix is a second authorization rule that reads a name, not a capability; it contradicts "enforced in one place, two surfaces" and makes the REST door the agent's only path to an entire object family — which is the opposite of the design goal and, as measured above, no safer.
3. **The gate stack that exists.** Author opt-in (`ai.exposed` + `ai.description`) → operator switch (ADR-0126 packaged-action activation) → caller's permission and RLS (ADR-0066 D4) → HITL confirmation for destructive acts (ADR-0011) → audit. Five layers, each carrying capability information. The blanket guard adds a sixth that carries none. Under option B nothing changes until an author writes `ai: { exposed: true, description }` on a specific action — and today zero do — so B is observably identical to A on day one, with the difference that the decision moves into reviewable metadata.
4. **Mainstream practice** (public documentation, not fetched in this session): Salesforce Agentforce exposes an action to an agent only when it is explicitly added to the agent, running under the agent user's permission set; Microsoft's Entra Agent ID / Copilot Studio model gives agents their own least-privilege identity and gates admin operations behind explicit connectors and approvals; the MCP specification carries per-tool annotations (`destructiveHint`, `readOnlyHint`) and expects hosts to confirm destructive tools with the user; OWASP's LLM / agentic guidance names "excessive agency" and prescribes least privilege plus human approval for high-impact actions. The common shape is **explicit per-capability enablement + least privilege + human confirmation for destructive acts** — neither "every admin object forbidden forever" nor "everything the API serves".
5. **AI error and prompt injection.** The agent-specific risk is an instruction smuggled into record content ("ban this user", "reset their password to…"). Under B an injected instruction cannot reach an action its own declaration does not expose, the HITL confirmation still stands in front of destructive acts, and the principal's permissions bound the rest; under C every `sys_*` action the REST door serves is one injected sentence away from an agent that holds an admin key; under A the same agent reaches them over REST anyway, so A is a parity loss, not a mitigation.
6. **Operational pull.** No customer names it on the board. The pull is the maintainer's design goal and the ordinary support automations an agent is asked for (revoke a stolen session, cancel a stale invitation, offboard a leaver). p1 by inheritance from #27506.
7. **Workload and evolution.** B: `domain:server` S–M — the runtime guard and the MCP guard yield to the per-action flag, `list_actions` parity, a dogfood case on one `sys_user` action; no new key. The per-action declarations are separate, later decisions, each one line of metadata under review.

### Options

| | What it does | Day-one effect | Risk shape | Workload |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **A** keep both refusals | `sys_*` stays off MCP; REST remains the agent's path | none | parity loss, no mitigation (same key reaches REST) | 0 |
| **B** per-action opt-in | both guards and the listing filter yield to `ai: { exposed: true }`; REST-door gates unchanged behind it | none until a declaration lands (0 today) | explicit, per action, reviewable; HITL confirmation stands | server S–M, 1 PR |
| **C** blanket lift | every `sys_*` action the REST door serves is listed and callable over MCP | all identity actions reachable by any admin-keyed agent | one injected sentence from account takeover | server S, 1 PR |
| **D** operator switch | `allowSystemObjects` made to reach the runtime guard; a deployment flips all `sys_*` on or off | none until an operator flips it | coarse: all or nothing, no per-action review; the flip is outside metadata and outside the audit of a PR | server S, 1 PR |

### Recommendation

**B, with three execution parameters named in the ruling:**
1. Both sites (`run_action` and `list_actions`) and both guards yield to the same per-action flag; no deployment-level bypass is added (D's switch stays where it is, MCP-side, default false, and gains no new reach).
2. **Declaration policy for this repository's `sys_*` actions:** each `ai.exposed` on a platform identity action is its own ruling of record, starting from zero; actions that mint a credential or a session — `impersonate_user`, `set_user_password`, API-key create / regenerate, SSO-provider writes — are not declared exposed without a maintainer ruling naming the action, and `ai.requiresConfirmation` is never set to false on them. (Policy, not code: it names what the platform-objects author may write.)
3. The audit row of an action run through MCP records the surface, so an administrator can tell an agent's call from a click without a second log.

Not A: it records the design goal as not covering `sys_*` and buys no security the REST door has not already spent. Not C: blanket exposure of credential-minting acts. Not D: an all-or-nothing operator switch is the per-action decision pushed to the least reviewable place.

Confidence gaps: whether `ai.requiresConfirmation`'s HITL path is wired for MCP-invoked actions end to end (ADR-0011 names it; the MCP arm was not exercised here — the dev measures it first and the PR shows the confirmation refusing an unconfirmed destructive call); the mainstream readings above are from public documentation, not pages fetched in this session.

os-decision-facets
① 长远：一套能力闸、两个面；按对象名前缀的笼统拒绝是第二套按名字的授权，与 ADR-0066 D4 和「agent 和人同一系统」相悖；B 让决定落在逐动作、可评审的元数据上
② 拉动：维护者设计目标 + #27649 已开放的 REST 身份动作；今天零个 sys_* 动作声明暴露，B 落地当天行为不变
③ 防错：注入的指令够不到未声明暴露的动作；破坏性动作仍过 HITL 确认；C 让铸造凭据的动作离注入一句话；A 不是缓解（同一把钥匙走 REST 照样能调）
④ 不扩散：不加键、不加门禁、不加部署开关；逐动作声明按拉动逐条来
